channel.title: Password Sense — VaultMesh
channel.description: Plain-English notes on password safety and account security, from the team behind VaultMesh.

item.title: The hidden account setting attackers configure after they get in
item.description: When someone gets into your email, they often don't just read it and leave — they set up a rule that keeps sending them your messages long after you've changed the password.

item.title: Two-step login and two-factor authentication are not the same thing
item.description: Sending a login code to your email is better than nothing — but it is not the same as true 2FA, and the difference matters for accounts you really need to protect.

item.title: Fake tech support calls: how they work and how to shut them down
item.description: The caller sounds professional and the problem sounds urgent — but one rule shuts down almost every tech support scam: hang up and call back on a number you looked up yourself.

item.title: What incognito mode actually does
item.description: Private browsing clears your local history when you close the window — but your ISP, employer, and every site you visit can still see exactly what you did.

item.title: What to do when you think your account has been hacked
item.description: If you suspect an account has been compromised, a few calm steps in the right order will do more than a panicked sweep of everything at once.

item.title: What end-to-end encrypted actually means
item.description: End-to-end encryption protects your messages from the service provider — but it has real limits that are worth understanding before you rely on it.

item.title: What a VPN actually protects you from (and what it doesn't)
item.description: VPNs are marketed as all-purpose security tools, but most of the threats people worry about are ones a VPN doesn't address at all.

item.title: Device encryption: why it matters when your phone goes missing
item.description: Full-device encryption means a thief who gets your phone can't read its contents without your PIN — but the protection is only as strong as that PIN.

item.title: How to find and fix your weakest passwords
item.description: Most people have a few dangerously weak passwords hiding among acceptable ones — here's how to find them and fix the ones that matter most.

item.title: Phishing by text: how SMS scams work and how to spot them
item.description: SMS scams use the same tricks as email phishing, but text messages feel more personal and urgent — which is exactly what makes them effective.

item.title: The apps still connected to your accounts
item.description: Every app you've connected to Google, Apple, or Microsoft keeps that access until you explicitly revoke it — and most people never do.

item.title: Backup codes: the 2FA safety net most people never save
item.description: When you set up 2FA, most services generate backup codes for emergencies — but skipping that step is how people get locked out of their own accounts.

item.title: Not all data breaches are the same
item.description: A breach notification doesn't always mean your password is at risk — how urgently you need to act depends on what was actually exposed.

item.title: What 'Sign in with Google' actually does to your account
item.description: Social login is convenient, but it makes your Google or Apple account a master key for every service you connect to it.

item.title: Passkeys: the sign-in method that doesn't use a password
item.description: Passkeys replace the password entirely — your device proves your identity with a cryptographic key that never leaves it.

item.title: How to share account access without sharing a password
item.description: Sending a password over text or email leaves it in message history permanently — there are cleaner ways to share account access.

item.title: Staying logged in: when it's fine and when it isn't
item.description: Persistent login sessions are convenient — but a liability on shared devices or when your screen isn't locked.

item.title: SIM swapping: when someone steals your phone number
item.description: A SIM swap attack transfers your phone number to someone else's device — and with it, any verification codes your accounts send via text.

item.title: The account settings most people never update
item.description: Your recovery email and phone number are what get you back in when something goes wrong — but most people set them once and never revisit them.

item.title: You don't need to change your password every 90 days
item.description: Forced password rotation leads to weaker passwords, not stronger ones — here's what current guidance actually says, and when you really should change a password.

item.title: Why your email account deserves more protection than anything else
item.description: Every "forgot password" link goes to your inbox — which makes your email account the recovery point for everything else you own online.

item.title: Four random words: the passphrase that's stronger than it looks
item.description: A four-word passphrase can be easier to remember than a complex password and harder to guess — but only if the words are chosen randomly.

item.title: Browser-saved passwords: convenient, but at what cost?
item.description: Letting your browser remember passwords is easy and reasonably secure in many cases — but there are real trade-offs worth knowing before you rely on it.

item.title: Public WiFi: what's a real risk and what isn't anymore
item.description: The old WiFi eavesdropping threat has shrunk considerably — here's what still matters and what you can mostly stop worrying about.

item.title: Why security questions are often the weakest link
item.description: Mother's maiden name and first pet — security questions feel like extra protection, but their answers are often findable by anyone who looks.

item.title: What a password manager actually does (and doesn't do)
item.description: Password managers are simpler than they sound — here's what they store, how the master password works, and what happens if you forget it.

item.title: Your password was in a breach — here's what actually matters next
item.description: Getting a breach notification is unsettling, but the right response is short and specific — not a security overhaul of every account you own.

item.title: Two-factor authentication, explained without jargon
item.description: What 2FA actually is, the three common kinds, and why SMS is weaker than the alternatives — but still worth using.

item.title: The one password habit that quietly hurts most people
item.description: Reusing the same password across multiple sites turns one compromised account into a key that unlocks all of them.

item.title: How to spot a phishing login page before you type
item.description: A few reliable cues — domain name, urgency, the padlock myth — that cover the most common phishing attempts before you enter a single character.

item.title: Strong passwords vs complex passwords — they're not the same
item.description: Symbols and uppercase letters feel like strength, but length and unpredictability are what actually make a password hard to guess.

item.title: A blog about the password habits that actually matter
item.description: A short note on what Password Sense is for, who it's written for, and what kinds of posts to expect.
